builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization
summary: MemSteer replaces costly human-annotated QA labels and supporting evidence with automatically generated, evidence-grounded QA supervision, which is then used to evaluate and iteratively revise memory store, retrieval, and context construction without updating model parameters. The cost is additional LLM inference for plan construction, question generation, source-grounded auditing, and blind answer recovery, plus the engineering complexity of an optimization loop around the memory system rather than a fixed retrieval pipeline. Failure modes include noisy or unfaithful synthetic QA pairs passing the audits, overfitting the memory design to generated supervision that does not match real user queries, and dependence on the quality of the underlying LLM used for annotation and diagnosis.
rationale: The method runs entirely at the prompting and retrieval-design level with no parameter updates, making it feasible on a 24 GB GPU or via APIs, but the reported gains are benchmark-specific and must be validated against the reader's own memory workload before production adoption.
technique: Synthetic QA supervision for agent memory optimization

claims.statement: MemSteer replaces costly human-annotated QA labels and supporting evidence with automatically generated, evidence-grounded QA supervision, which is then used to evaluate and iteratively revise memory store, retrieval, and context construction without updating model parameters. The cost is additional LLM inference for plan construction, question generation, source-grounded auditing, and blind answer recovery, plus the engineering complexity of an optimization loop around the memory system rather than a fixed retrieval pipeline. Failure modes include noisy or unfaithful synthetic QA pairs passing the audits, overfitting the memory design to generated supervision that does not match real user queries, and dependence on the quality of the underlying LLM used for annotation and diagnosis.

MemSteer-Opt improves ATM-Bench Question Score by 13.4 points and RHELM accuracy by 4.1 and 6.6 points (without and with external data) relative to Base-BM25, competitive with official-QA-guided optimization.
